hero.lead: FORGE-120 is a 120-day hands-on learning path.
hero.detail: You start with Linux, Git and networking. Then you move to cloud, CI, Terraform and Kubernetes. Later you learn reliability and safe AI tool use.
hero.because: AI comes later because you should understand your system before depending on a model.

fixtureLabel: Fixed example. Not a live model, and not a live index.

phase-01.plain: Linux, Git, HTTP, DNS, and how you record what you actually saw.

phase-02.plain: Azure networks, private access, DNS and identity.

phase-03.plain: Pipelines, artifacts, and how a change gets delivered.

phase-04.plain: Terraform, a small application, and Docker.

phase-05.plain: Workloads, networking, storage and troubleshooting on Kubernetes.

phase-06.plain: AKS networking, container registry, identity and monitoring.

phase-07.plain: Terraform modules, Helm, promotion and rollback.

phase-08.plain: Change gates, measurements, alerts and incidents.

phase-09.plain: Retrieval, citations, evaluation, and checks before a tool runs.

phase-10.plain: Architecture, trade-offs, and a closed-note review.

items.name: Linux
items.plain: Use the machine from the command line.

items.name: Git
items.plain: Track changes and recover work safely.

items.name: Networking
items.plain: See how a request moves between machines.

items.name: Azure
items.plain: Put a network and an identity in the cloud.

items.name: Terraform
items.plain: Create cloud infrastructure from code.

items.name: Docker
items.plain: Package an application so it runs the same way.

items.name: Kubernetes
items.plain: Run and manage containers reliably.

items.name: AKS
items.plain: Run Kubernetes on Azure.

items.name: CI/CD
items.plain: Build and deliver a change the same way each time.

items.name: Monitoring
items.plain: Notice when the system is unhealthy.

items.name: Reliability
items.plain: Decide what good looks like before you are on call.

items.name: Incidents
items.plain: Respond from evidence, then write down what happened.

items.name: Rollback
items.plain: Return to a known good version.

items.name: Debugging
items.plain: Find the failing part with a recorded observation.

items.name: RAG
items.plain: Answer from retrieved text, not from memory alone.

items.name: Retrieval
items.plain: Find the useful parts of a source before answering.

items.name: Citations
items.plain: Show which source the answer came from.

items.name: Policy checks
items.plain: A fixed check decides what is allowed. A prompt does not.

items.name: MCP
items.plain: A tool connection the policy can allow or refuse.

items.name: Evaluation
items.plain: Compare the output with an expected result.

items.name: Controlled tools
items.plain: The model may call only a tool the policy allowed.

order.name: Kubernetes and AKS
order.plain: Workloads need a place to run and a way to recover.

order.name: Reliability
order.plain: Systems fail. You practise noticing and recording.

order.name: RAG and controlled tool use
order.plain: AI should work inside clear boundaries.

days.name: Read
days.plain: Understand the words. Predict what will happen before you run it.

days.name: Try
days.plain: Do the task yourself. On write days, the first version is yours.

days.name: Break
days.plain: Break one thing safely. Write down what you saw.

days.name: Debug
days.plain: Evidence goes in a file. A chat is not evidence.

days.name: Practise
days.plain: Answer out loud, including the case that fails.

days.name: Review
days.plain: If you cannot explain it, you do not own it yet.

retrieval.name: Source
retrieval.plain: Start from a document you are willing to trust.

retrieval.name: Chunk
retrieval.plain: Split that document into smaller pieces.

retrieval.name: Retrieve
retrieval.plain: The system finds the useful parts of the source before the model answers.

retrieval.name: Context
retrieval.plain: Those parts are handed to the model with the question.

retrieval.name: Cite
retrieval.plain: The answer points at the source. If it cannot, it should not pretend.

control.name: Request
control.plain: A person asks for something the service is allowed to do.

control.name: Model
control.plain: The model proposes a next step. It does not skip the checks.

control.name: Policy
control.plain: A fixed rule decides what is allowed. Another prompt does not.

control.name: Validation
control.plain: The proposed tool must match a known schema and an allowlist.

control.name: Tool
control.plain: Only the allowed tool runs. An unknown shell does not.

control.name: Result
control.plain: The tool returns evidence. The model does not invent that evidence.

control.name: Evaluation
control.plain: Compare the output with a known expected result.

control.name: Audit
control.plain: Record the path. A switch can stop it.

spans.name: Understand and operate the system
spans.plain: Days 1–96. Learn the machine, the cloud, delivery, Kubernetes and reliability before a model is in the path.

spans.name: Retrieval, policy, controlled tools and evaluation
spans.plain: Days 97–105. Retrieval, citations, policy, evaluation and tools that can be refused.

spans.name: Design and defence
spans.plain: Days 106–120. Architecture, trade-offs and a closed-note review.
